Trump’s recent remarks have added a new geopolitical dimension to the campaign. Polling cited by international outlets indicates that many Greenlanders support eventual independence from Denmark, while most do not favor becoming part of the United States. Even so, the renewed attention from Washington has elevated questions about sovereignty, security and economic leverage in the Arctic.

With six parties competing for 31 seats in parliament, the result is being closely watched as an indicator of whether Greenland’s voters favor a faster push toward independence or a more cautious approach under continued Danish oversight. With 1.3 million people currently covered by temporary protected status nationwide, the case is being seen as a defining test of whether the court will side with executive power over humanitarian safeguards.
